findings.title: Login cache is over-invalidated because wrapped isEnabled() on idpById returns false whenever the linked org is currently disabled
findings.body: In registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated), the `original` argument is `idpById` from getById(model.getInternalId()), which is wrapped via createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(...) and overrides isEnabled() to additionally check the linked organization's runtime status (provider.isEnabled() && org.isEnabled() && super.isEnabled()). The `updated` argument is the raw model passed to update(...), whose isEnabled() only reflects the model's ENABLED field. When the IDP is linked to an org that is currently disabled or removed, getLoginPredicate().test(original) returns false (wrapped isEnabled returns false because of the org status), while getLoginPredicate().test(updated) returns true (raw isEnabled is true). Neither early-return branch matches, so the login cache is invalidated even though the update did not change the IDP's static login configuration. The cache state would still be functionally correct (the wrapped isEnabled at read time filters out the IDP), so the impact is wasted work rather than incorrect results, but the optimization described in the Javadoc ('IDP is currently a login IDP' vs 'currently NOT a login IDP') is undermined for org-linked IDPs. Consider obtaining the underlying model for the comparison (e.g., look up cached via realmCache.getCache().get(internalId, CachedIdentityProvider.class) or idpDelegate.getById) rather than the org-aware wrapped instance.

findings.title: Misleading comment in remove(): comment refers to a cache lookup that actually goes to the JPA delegate
findings.body: The comment '//lookup idp by alias in cache to be able to invalidate its internalId' sits next to the use of `storedIdp`, which is populated from idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) — i.e. a JPA delegate lookup, not a cache lookup. The refactor hoisted idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) out of the `if (isInvalid(cacheKey))` branch into a local variable used by both branches of the if/else, but the wording still implies a cache read. The lookup never consults the cache.

findings.title: testCacheIDPForLogin registers removal of an IDP with alias 'alias' (literal) instead of the alias variable
findings.body: In the loop creating IDPs the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)`. The argument is the literal string "alias", not the loop variable (e.g. `alias`). This will attempt to remove an IDP with alias "alias" at cleanup time, which does not exist. The pattern is pre-existing in testCacheIDPByOrg, but the PR copies it into the new test instead of fixing it. The fix is to use `alias` (the variable) rather than the literal string.

findings.title: testCacheIDPForLogin does not cover organization-level changes that affect login availability
findings.body: The new test exercises IDP create/remove/update and the cache invalidations they cause. It does not exercise organization-level changes that affect IDP login availability: disabling an organization, removing an organization, or unlinking an IDP from its organization. None of these trigger registerIDPLoginInvalidation/OnUpdate, so the login cache may stay stale until some unrelated IDP change triggers an invalidation. The wrapped isEnabled() at read time filters out IDPs whose org is disabled, so correctness is preserved, but the cache freshness behavior in those scenarios is untested.
